pool.text: Without using a calculator, evaluate \(52^2 - 48^2\).

Compute the difference \(52 - 48 = 4\) and the sum \(52 + 48 = 100\).
Multiply those two factors together to obtain the exact integer value.

pool.domain: GAT Ratios, Percentages, Work & Motion Problems
pool.text: A driver travels a \(60\text{ km}\) route from Riyadh to a research station at \(30\text{ km/h}\) and returns along the exact same route at \(60\text{ km/h}\). What is the average speed for the entire round trip?
pool.sol: Round-trip average speed over equal distances is the harmonic mean \(v_{\text{avg}} = \frac{2 v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2} = \frac{2(30)(60)}{30 + 60} = 40\text{ km/h}\).
hints: Average speed is total distance divided by total time — never the simple arithmetic mean when speeds differ.
Use the Qiyas round-trip harmonic formula \(v_{\text{avg}} = \frac{2 v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2}\).
Substitute \(v_1 = 30\) and \(v_2 = 60\) and simplify the fraction.

pool.sol: Round-trip average speed over equal distances is the harmonic mean \(v_{\text{avg}} = \frac{2 v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2} = \frac{2(90)(180)}{90 + 180} = 120\text{ km/h}\).
hints: Average speed is total distance divided by total time — never the simple arithmetic mean when speeds differ.
Use the Qiyas round-trip harmonic formula \(v_{\text{avg}} = \frac{2 v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2}\).
Substitute \(v_1 = 90\) and \(v_2 = 180\) and simplify the fraction.

pool.domain: GAT Ratios, Percentages, Work & Motion Problems
pool.text: Pump A can fill tank #1 alone in \(3\) hours, and Pump B can fill the same tank alone in \(6\) hours. Working together at their constant rates, how many hours will it take to fill the empty tank?
pool.sol: Combined rate is \(\frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{6} = \frac{9}{18}\), so total time is \(T = \frac{t_1 t_2}{t_1 + t_2} = 2\) hours.
hints: Add hourly work rates \(\frac{1}{t_1} + \frac{1}{t_2}\), not the times themselves.
Combine \(\frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{6}\) over a common denominator.
Take the reciprocal of the combined hourly rate to get the total hours needed.

pool.text: What is the fundamental period of the trigonometric function \(y = 2\cos(2x) + 1\)?

pool.text: A particle's position along a line is \(s(t) = 1t^3 - 2t^2 + 3t\) meters at time \(t\) seconds. What is its instantaneous velocity at \(t = 1\text{ s}\)?
